$comment: The results archive: which lifters are mirrored out of a public bulk dataset of
every federation on earth, and the bounds that stop a parser regression from
publishing a fraction of it and calling that a build.
This file names no rows and transcribes no figures. Unlike every other document
in `data/sources/`, it is not a reading of a published table -- it is the scope
rule applied to somebody else's dataset, plus the credit their licence asks for.
The adapter is `packages/ingestion/src/sources/athlete-mirror.ts` and its header
carries the measurements the numbers below were chosen against.
WHY THE MIRROR IS SCOPED AT ALL
The archive is roughly four million entries. Projected to the columns this
collection uses it comes to about 1.4 GB of JSON, which exceeds what the
hosting publishes in total, before a single record shard is counted. So the
mirror holds every entry of every lifter with at least one entry under the
federations named in `scope` -- 593,144 entries across 94,236 lifters when
measured against the 2026-08-01 archive, about 217 MB.
Note which half of that is generous. The audience is narrow on purpose; what a
lifter inside it gets is complete. Somebody who spent five years in another
federation before their first USPA meet sees those five years, because a
qualifying total is a qualifying total wherever it was lifted.
A lifter outside the scope is told plainly that nothing was found and is given
the manual route, which stays fully usable on its own. That is what makes the
scope a speed decision rather than a correctness one.
WHY THERE IS NO `sha256` HERE
For the same reason the record snapshot has none: the upstream archive is
rebuilt whenever a meet is entered, so a digest would have to be re-cut every
week and would stop being a decision anybody made. What replaces it is the pair
of bounds below and the adapter's own refusals -- a header missing a column, a
date that is not a date, a weight that is not a weight. A meet weekend passes
all of them; a schema change upstream does not.
WHY THE ARCHIVE IS NOT COMMITTED
It is 816 MB extracted. It is downloaded to a gitignored `.cache/` and the
publisher reads it from there, which is why this is the one source with no
snapshot beside it. Publication is off unless the build is pointed at a copy;
see `packages/ingestion/src/bin/publish-data.ts`.
label: Competition results archive

$comment:attribution: The sample attribution text from the archive's own LICENSE.txt, verbatim. The
data is public domain and the credit is requested rather than required, which
is precisely why it is worth getting exactly right and worth carrying in data:
a build that changes the data must not be able to leave an old credit on the
page. Published as its own field of the mirror artifact and printed beside the
provenance.attribution: This page uses data from the OpenPowerlifting project, https://www.openpowerlifting.org.

$comment:scope: Two lists, because the archive distinguishes the body that sanctioned a meet
from the body it answers to. An affiliate names itself in `Federation` and its
parent in `ParentFederation`, so matching only the first misses every
international meet and matching only the second misses every meet run by a
federation the archive files as its own parent.
These are exact string matches against the archive's own spelling, not against
any identifier this project publishes. They are the archive's vocabulary and
changing one changes who is in the mirror, which is why they are here and not
scopeNote: Lifters with at least one result under USPA or an IPL-affiliated federation. Their whole competitive history is shown, including meets held under other federations. A lifter who has never entered a USPA or IPL meet will not be found here; enter your figures by hand instead.
$comment:bounds: A floor and a ceiling, both measured against the 2026-08-01 archive and both
with room in them. Neither is an expected value: an exact count would fail
every week for being right, unattended, with nobody there to tell it so.
`minimumEntries` catches the failure that is otherwise invisible -- a scope or
projection rule that quietly stops matching produces a valid artifact that is
simply mostly empty, and on the site that reads as a quiet month upstream. The
measured figure is 593,144; a build that finds under 400,000 has a bug rather
`maximumWithheldRows` is the other direction. 4,914 of the in-scope rows carry
a name written in a script that folds to no Latin letters at all, which is a
real property of an international archive and not a defect -- those lifters are
unreachable by any spelling a lookup box can produce, so they are withheld with
a count rather than published under a key nobody can type. The budget is set
well above that so a genuine parser break -- a shifted column, a changed date
format -- fails the build instead of arriving as a quietly thinner mirror.
